ai_technology: Donor-resolved non-smooth non-negative matrix factorization; cross-donor consensus gene-program discovery

evidence.ai_role: NMF learned additive gene-expression programs separately in donor/cell-type units; cross-donor consensus construction identified recurring programs before outcome testing. This learned program discovery, rather than visualization or dimensionality reduction alone, enabled the fixed beta-cell signature and its subsequent functional association tests.
evidence.tested: Program discovery used 48 donors. Primary independent single-cell validation used 55 eligible HPAP donors, with additional pooled Smart-seq2 and bulk analyses. Functional associations used 52 UPenn and 42 Vanderbilt donors, of whom 39 overlapped; higher frozen program scores tracked stimulated insulin release after diagnosis and preparation-quality adjustments.
evidence.unknown: Existing-data associations are retrospective and do not establish that the program causes secretory dysfunction. Two laboratories largely measured the same donors; bulk cell-composition adjustment was not robust across platforms. Patient-level clinical utility, causal perturbation and independent biological replication remain unestablished.

organization: Jinggangshan University; The Chinese University of Hong Kong; Shenzhen University of Advanced Technology; Shenzhen People’s Hospital

source_review.scope: Primary 71-page preprint PDF relevant donor-resolved NMF and consensus construction Methods, fixed-score validation and matched perifusion Methods/Results, and limitations; cached primary bioRxiv v1 metadata. Supplements not exhaustively audited.

summary: A November 24, 2026 preprint used donor-resolved non-negative matrix factorization and consensus program discovery to identify a beta-cell gene program reduced in type 2 diabetes. Learned program definitions were fixed before testing in other datasets. Higher program scores were associated with greater stimulated insulin release in donor-matched measurements from two laboratories. The laboratories shared most donors, so these are complementary measurements rather than independent biological replications, and the association does not establish a causal mechanism or treatment target.
title: Unsupervised program learning links a beta-cell signature to insulin secretion
